english.title: Cause / aggravate / prolong injury to another intending to cause him / her to avoid service in the armed forces
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowing that another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), was subject to service law and intending to cause

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

to avoid service

(C)_[caused him an injury]_
(D)_[caused her an injury]_
(E)_[aggravated or prolonged an injury of that person]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 345(2) and (7) of the Armed Forces Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing that another person was subject to service law
intending to cause him/her to avoid service
caused him/her injury/aggravated/prolonged an injury of that person

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 345(4) of the Armed Forces Act 2006 provides that the offence applies to any act done in a relevant territory (the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man or a British overseas territory); or otherwise than in a relevant territory, by a United Kingdom national or a person resident in a relevant territory.
(ii) Section 345(6) of the Act provides the meaning of injury and service.
(iii) See section 347 of the Act if the offence was committed outside the United Kingdom.
(iv) This offence may be committed by non military individuals who may be dealt with by a non military court.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Imprisonment not exceeding twelve months and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
INDICTMENT: Imprisonment not exceeding two years and/or fine.

Time limit for prosecution:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
